subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should builtin memory-core add durable checkpoint/resume for forced/full reindex operations, and should that behavior be automatic, shadow-DB based, or exposed through memorySearch config?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the repair changes durable memory index generation state, safe-publish semantics, and possibly public configuration, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Sponsor automatic resume
options.body: Implement resume by default in memory-core with SQLite-backed generation/checkpoint state while preserving the safe publish invariant and adding status/docs/tests for incomplete generations.

options.title: Use explicit opt-in config
options.body: Add documented memorySearch indexing controls such as resume and checkpoint intervals with upgrade proof for default compatibility and opt-in behavior.

options.title: Defer resume work
options.body: Keep all-or-nothing rebuilds for now and focus only on narrower metadata durability, stale-shadow cleanup, retries, and clearer operator status.

recommendation.title: Sponsor automatic resume
recommendation.body: Implement resume by default in memory-core with SQLite-backed generation/checkpoint state while preserving the safe publish invariant and adding status/docs/tests for incomplete generations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history on the reindex architecture and prior review context for this exact issue.
